mcat_description.short: Prefabricated wooden houses are factory-built or site-assembled residential and hospitality structures made primarily from structural timber, engineered wood, or log construction, sold as complete turnkey units or panel kits in India.
mcat_description.long: Wooden houses in the Indian B2B market are prefabricated or semi-prefabricated structures constructed using structural timber (pine, cedar, SPF), engineered wood (glulam, LVL), or log construction methods, designed for permanent residential use, resort accommodation, farmhouses, and eco-tourism retreats. The dominant construction typologies include A-frame cottages, log cabins, post-and-beam homes, and modular panel-frame structures, all manufactured in a factory environment and assembled on-site on an RCC or steel plinth foundation. Key differentiators in the Indian market include wood species and grade (imported SPF/pine vs. local timber), construction method (log vs. timber frame vs. engineered wood panel), floor area, number of bedrooms, and treatment specifications (termite, waterproofing, fire retardant). Buyers range from individual landowners seeking eco-friendly residences to resort developers and hospitality operators procuring multiple units for glamping, boutique resorts, and hill-station retreats.

market_context: The Indian prefabricated wooden house market is served by a growing ecosystem of specialist manufacturers concentrated in Delhi NCR, Bengaluru, Pune, and Goa, supplying structures across all Indian climate zones from Himalayan hill stations to coastal Goa. The dominant construction typologies are A-frame cottages, log cabins, and timber frame panel homes, with imported SPF (Spruce-Pine-Fir) and Canadian pine being the most commonly used structural wood species, typically PEFC or FSC certified. Engineered wood variants (glulam, LVL) are used by premium manufacturers for dimensional stability and seismic performance. Key BIS standards governing structural timber in Indian buildings include IS:883 (Design of Structural Timber in Building — Code of Practice) and IS:3629 (Specification for Structural Timber in Building). The hospitality and eco-tourism segment (resort cottages, glamping pods, boutique hotel cabins) is the fastest-growing buyer segment, with manufacturers like Loom Crafts, Vrisa Innovation, Deodar Log Homes, Royal Prefab, and WoodenHousing all explicitly targeting resort developers. Prefab wooden houses offer 30–50% faster construction timelines than conventional masonry and are positioned as eco-friendly, sustainable alternatives. Treatment specifications (termite treatment, waterproofing, fire retardant coating) are critical differentiators in the Indian market given tropical humidity and monsoon conditions. The unit of transaction is universally per square foot in Indian B2B dealings.
